title: Application of a high-throughput swarm-based deep neural network Algorithm reveals SPAG5 downregulation as a potential therapeutic target in adult AML.
authors: Ajonu, Chinyere I; Grundy, Robert I; Ball, Graham R; Zafeiris, Dimitrios
one_liner_zh: 该文用群智能深度神经网络分析AML转录组，聚焦SPAG5与MDM2/CDK1基因互作，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅基因表达网络分析，与本课题无关。
abstract: Gene‒gene interactions play pivotal roles in disease pathogenesis and are fundamental in the development of targeted therapeutics, particularly through the elucidation of oncogenic gene drivers in cancer. The systematic analysis of pathways and gene interactions is critical in the drug discovery process for various cancer subtypes. SPAG5, known for its role in spindle formation during cell division, has been identified as an oncogene in several cancers, although its specific impact on AML remains underexplored. This study leverages a high-throughput swarm-based deep neural network (SDNN) and transcriptomic data-an approach that enhances predictive accuracy and robustness through collective intelligence-to augment, model, and enhance the understanding of the TP53 pathway in AML cohorts. Our integrative systems biology approach identified SPAG5 as a uniquely downregulated driver in adult AML, underscoring its potential as a novel therapeutic target. The interaction of SPAG5 with key hub genes such as MDM2 and CDK1 not only reinforces its role in tumour suppression through negative regulation but also highlights its potential in moderating the phenotypic and genomic alterations associated with AML progression. This study of the role and interaction dynamics of SPAG5 sets the stage for future research aimed at developing targeted and personalized treatment approaches for AML, utilizing the capabilities of genetic interventions.
abstract_zh: 基因-基因相互作用在疾病发病机制中扮演关键角色，并且是开发靶向治疗的基础，尤其是在癌症中通过阐明致癌基因驱动因子方面。对通路和基因相互作用的系统分析在多种癌症亚型的药物发现过程中至关重要。SPAG5，已知在细胞分裂期间参与纺锤体形成，已在多种癌症中被鉴定为致癌基因，尽管其对急性髓系白血病（AML）的具体影响仍未充分探索。本研究利用高通量基于群体的深度神经网络（SDNN）和转录组数据——一种通过集体智能增强预测准确性和稳健性的方法——来增强、建模并提升对AML队列中TP53通路理解。我们的整合系统生物学方法将SPAG5鉴定为成人AML中独特下调的驱动因子，强调其作为新型治疗靶点的潜力。SPAG5与关键枢纽基因如MDM2和CDK1的相互作用不仅通过负调控强化了其在肿瘤抑制中的作用，还突显了其在调节与AML进展相关的表型和基因组改变中的潜力。本研究对SPAG5的作用及相互作用动态的探索，为未来旨在利用遗传干预能力开发针对AML的靶向和个性化治疗方法奠定了基础。
